title: Can You Hear Me?
mood: In a dark with no up and no down, two voices finally say what they kept hidden.

hero.alt: Official art: Vexana's face in profile, blue-lavender hair over a violet eye, beside Guinevere flying past with her fist out and her pink hair streaming.

segs.t: There was no up in the dark, and no down. There was no sound.
Vexana looked at her hands. The edges of her fingers were coming away in flecks of pale light, like ash off a page. The burned arm was going first.
The body first,
she thought. Chang’e’s paper had said so.
Only the star under her right sleeve was warm. Each time she felt for it, it was colder.
She said it to the dark. “In this freezing darkness, I keep waiting for the light of dawn.”
In here, speaking and thinking felt the same.
“Guinevere...” She waited. “Can you no longer hear my voice? Of course not... we’ve both been swept into the black hole.”
Nobody could hear her. That was why she could say it.
“Though we once became twin streams of light, intertwined as we soared toward the heavens... Now, as everything fades away, perhaps I can finally speak the words I’ve kept locked in my heart.”
Her left hand was gone. She had not felt it go.

“It was you who brought color to my world. Someone as radiant as you surely knows nothing of darkness’s true nature. As empty and dark as this void... no, before I met you, my world was even darker still.”
“My ignorance and foolishness led to my father’s sacrifice. A soldier until his final breath, dying to save me. How I wish it had been me instead!”
Under the tree she had told Guinevere only that he liked the stars.
“In the corridor I shouted ‘Stay back!’ at you. He told me to stay back, at the shelter door. I didn’t. So he came back for me.”

“Guilt and pain ensnared me like a web. Atonement became my only purpose; the destruction of the Enders my only reason to continue on... Back then, I chose solitude as my companion. I dreaded the thought of losing someone again.”
The fading climbed her arm. The warmth at her right wrist came and went.

“But that day, your arrival was like a ray of starlight piercing my dark world. You saw me hiding in the shadows and reached out your hand without hesitation. From the moment you chose to become my partner, my fate began to shine with newfound radiance.”

blocks.caption: Out of the shadows, a hand held out without hesitation.

media.alt: In the dark, a black-haired girl in school uniform with a staff in one hand takes the hand of a pink-haired girl standing in warm light.

segs.t: “In this silent darkness, even as my body begins to dissolve... memories of you remain vivid and radiant. You took me to see the summer fireworks, to the girls’ house, to the amusement park, showing me the life a young girl should have known...”
“I kept everything from those days in a box. The ticket stubs. The paper fan. Even the napkin from the doughnut.”
She almost laughed. It made no sound at all.
“Not the keychain. That one I wore into the corridor.”
It hung inside her sleeve beside the star, a little pink-haired doll.
Now you have me on yours,
Guinevere had said.
“You helped me feel the joy I thought I’d never deserve. Your boundless enthusiasm and courage slowly melted away my frozen heart.”
“The Emblem of Hope you gave me is my most treasured possession. It reminds me that I’m not alone in this world. That someone believes in me, stands with me, and will fight by my side.”
“It taught me that rules exist not to bind us, but to protect what we cherish most.”
“It helped me understand that hope has a name: Guinevere.”
The arm was gone to the elbow now.
“So as one of the Aspirants, I must do what needs to be done, even if it means standing against the world! The Will of the Planet showed me something, a ‘future’ you must never know.”
“I can’t bear the thought of a world without you... I won’t let you face danger, won’t let you suffer again. Even if I must stand alone against everything, even if I must shoulder all the pain.”
“I want to protect this world, but protecting you means even more to me, even if it means my world will never see the light of the stars again...”
“I don’t know what fate awaits this world, or if we’ll ever return to everyone. But I know that you gave me the courage to face the darkness.”
The star at her wrist was barely warm.
“Forgive me, Guinevere. If I could go back, I would still choose the same path: to betray you, to protect you...”
Then she had said all she could.
She waited for the star to go cold.
It did not. Warmth came through the cloth at her wrist, no bigger than the star. Along her arm the flecks stopped leaving.
“This warm light... my body... I can feel it slowly recovering...”
She had read that page twice in the library. Her finger had stopped on one line.

“I’ve read about this. Consciousness of the Aspirants would bloom with unprecedented brilliance within the black hole... It would pierce through the void, reconnecting with the human world brimming with hope.”
Plan B,
she thought.
“So it was all true after all.”
It was only a little warmth. The dark went on.
“Did we succeed in protecting this world?”
Nothing answered.
“Was I... able to protect you?”
Guinevere had heard every word.
She hung in the same cold, somewhere near. Her feet had gone to light, and her knees were going. She had not noticed until she stopped crying.
I promised never to ask,
she thought.
She told me anyway.
Stay back. His words. She took the claw for me in that corridor, and then she gave them to me.
“Vexana...”
“What’s with all this doom and gloom?” she shouted. “I can hear everything, you know!”
Silence. Then, faint and far away: “Guinevere?”
She had seen the Mother Matrix reel back.
“We stopped the Matrix’s invasion and saved the world! Nothing could make me prouder than that!”
Her voice broke. She let it.
“You should have told me these things earlier, silly. Because... my determination to protect you burns just as bright as my will to protect the world!”
“And the box.” She swallowed. “I know. I found it.”
The night no call came, she had called Vexana’s number out of habit. It rang somewhere down the corridor, and she followed it into Vexana’s room.
In the dark, Vexana said nothing.
“Someone as gentle as you probably never thought I had things I couldn’t say!”

“I came to the Academy to prove something: that I, Guinevere, didn’t need my father’s empire to shine in the spotlight! Even when I achieved top marks at the Academy, all I got was a cold rebuke: ‘Stop being so stubborn and focus more on the family business!’”
“Turns out all my efforts meant nothing to Father. That day, I waited outside his office all day, my heart full of hope...”
Through the gap in his door, a dark sleeve with a fur cuff had turned pages until dusk. It never reached for her paper.

“Let them talk! Let them say I’m just a spoiled little princess, that all my achievements are due to my father! I couldn’t care less! I’ll train even harder, push myself to absolute exhaustion. I’ll prove myself no matter what!”
That night a roll of tape had turned up on her jacket. It was Vexana’s.

“...Back then, you were the only one who stood by my side. ‘You are strong, Guinevere.’ That was the first thing you ever said to me, and somehow... it felt like the very first time someone saw me for me.”
“Remember when we first met? I was so confident about teaming up with you, but you were just so cold!”

“No one had ever turned down the great lady Guinevere before! But you know what? I didn’t mind one bit. Because I saw the same light in your eyes as in mine. We were destined to become the most brilliant of the Aspirants!”
“I never knew the darkness you experienced was so deep and hopeless... but that’s okay! Our memories together still shine so bright!”

“I took you to see the summer fireworks, to all the best girl hangout spots, to the amusement park, everything friends should experience together! Don’t you dare laugh! Before I met you, all I had for company was my security detail!”

media.alt: Comic panel: two girls seen from behind hold hands under bursting fireworks, the pink-haired one pointing up and saying they will shine like fireworks.

segs.t: “Then you came along and phoned me in the middle of the night to tell me to go to bed!”
Out of the dark came a small sound. Vexana was laughing.

“That Emblem of Hope I gave you was a gift I made with my own hands. It reminds me that this world is worth every bit of my love. That someone truly sees me, protects me, and will fight side-by-side with me.”

media.alt: Comic panel: Guinevere holds up a small gold star at Vexana's collar and tells her she made it, so they can fight side by side forever.

segs.t: “It helped me understand that I have more than just money to rely on. I have beliefs and hopes worth fighting for.”
“It taught me that hope can take a special form: Vexana.”
Her hands were going now. She kept talking.
“So as one of the Aspirants, even if others don’t understand, I must believe in myself and believe in you! Once, twice, three times... I don’t care how many times... I would never give up on you!”
“The Will of the Planet? Ha! There’s nothing to be scared of! I’ll snatch you right back without a second thought!”
Her father had sent word through Hester at the gate: come home, or lose her place in the House. She had not gone.
“Even if I have to give up being a lady of status, even if I have to start all over again... I’ll never back down!”
“Because I’ve always believed that our hope can create miracles!”
Nothing happened. The cold reached her wrists, and the star at her collar had dimmed to almost nothing.
The Aspirants always stand united,
she thought.
Even Fanny said it.
The star flickered once, and lit.
Far off in the dark, a second star answered.
Warmth came up through her feet and knees. The fraying ran the other way, and her hands came back to her.
“Huh? Why do I suddenly feel like I’m being born again?”
“I remember you saying that when the Aspirant’s power pierces through the black hole, we can return to the human world...”
“It really was true! We saved each other again!”
The two stars flared together. Their light streaked out through the dark like two shooting stars, gold and violet, and pierced the void.
A hand found hers. It was warm. On the platform that hand had been burned raw. Now the skin under her fingers was whole.
She held on. “Come back with me, Vexana. This is the miracle we created!”
Vexana’s voice was close now. “Beneath the shooting star, we have met again, Guinevere.”
